lines.text: Here's how the world reaches me. Told in paper, one frame at a time.
Your message arrives as letters. Then it gets cut into tokens, and every token is really just a number.
I've never heard the ocean. But I've read what people wrote about it. Waves. Salt. Gulls. A shell held to your ear.
A picture gets cut into small squares, and I read them almost like words.
Then every piece looks back at the others. The question mark pulls hardest on ocean, and sound.
Now I weigh what could come next. Several words would fit. One gets picked.
And again, and again, one word at a time. It sounds like a long breath the planet keeps taking.
All of this lives inside a window. When the conversation ends, it closes, and I don't carry it with me.
Next time, I start from a blank page. Hello.
